card.title: ŌITA REGIMENT
card.text: Gets +1+1 when a Destruction effect triggers.
card.flavorText: The 47th Infantry Regiment was part of the 48th Division, one of the most mobile and combat ready formations in the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. Established in 1940, the 48th Division was formed from existing garrison and line units, including the 47th Regiment, which had become available after the reorganization of the 6th Division. In 1941, it was mechanized alongside the 5th Division, an uncommon upgrade that reflected its planned role in early Pacific campaigns. The division deployed to the Philippines in December 1941 as part of the 14th Army. It landed at Lingayen Gulf and advanced rapidly, capturing Manila in early January 1942. Soon afterward, the division was sent to Java in the Dutch East Indies, where it seized Surabaya and its critical oil infrastructure on 7 March 1942.The 48th was then transferred to Timor, where it fought against entrenched Australian and Dutch commandos in a difficult guerrilla campaign. Despite local resistance and challenging terrain, the Japanese secured the island by the end of 1942. Unlike many other units that were redeployed, the 48th Division remained on Timor as a garrison force for the remainder of the war, ultimately surrendering to Allied forces on the island in August 1945.
